doc.title: Buddy Collette interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999

title: The Town Hall big band and Mingus stopping every piece
summary: He lists the star lineup and tells how Mingus stopped each piece, threatened to quit, and was talked round.

bands.name: Charles Mingus Town Hall big band

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: So we played the first number in that big band. What a band. You probably heard the line up. Probably Eddie Bert and—

Yeah Clark and Snooky Young, Ernie Royal, Bernie Glow, trombones Britt Woodman, Butter Jackson — I can’t think of the other trombone player — but all the great guys. In the reed section there was Jerome Richardson, Phil Woods, Pepper Adams, Eric Dolphy, I was there, on and on.

But it was a great band, but he stopped every piece. He didn’t record anything through. And he said, “I wouldn’t buy that would you?” He asked the audience. And we were being baffled too because we had no control. You know when a leader stops you, that’s it.
I can’t imagine, you guys just kind of looking at each other going oh, what are we doing here.

Yeah. And I think the guys felt too if I was there, a lot of this stuff wouldn’t happen. That was the first time he kind of got me caught in it. But I knew if I’d go there things could happen see? Because I had no control. A lot of times I could talk to him on the side and say let’s don’t do this. He’d threatened to quit at the rehearsals three nights in a row because he said, “I don’t want to do this because I don’t want to do a concert.” And Jerome and I would go and have breakfast with him and we’d talk to him and after we’d talk to him he’d be okay that next day. But it was rough. © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-
